Domino drift effect (DDE) detector

Source: R/dfr_dde.R
dfr_dde.Rd

Feature drift detector that monitors only a subset of the features and estimates the probability that each of the other features drifts, from the correlation between the features (Szucs and Nemeth, 2025). The method relies on the domino drift effect: when features drift together, the neighbours (strongly correlated features) of a drifting feature are more likely to drift as well.

Usage

dfr_dde(
  target_feat = NULL,
  monitored = NULL,
  n_monitored = NULL,
  test = "js",
  threshold = NULL,
  window_size = 500,
  monitoring_step = 1,
  confirmation_delay = NULL,
  thresholds = seq(0, 0.9, by = 0.1),
  score_threshold = 0.5,
  update_curve = TRUE,
  delta = 2e-05,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

target_feat

Names of the features. NULL (the default) uses every numeric column.

monitored

Names of the monitored features, \(S_{check}\).

n_monitored

Number of monitored features, drawn at random when monitored is NULL. When both are NULL every feature is monitored and no score is predicted.

test

Univariate drift test applied to each monitored feature: one of "js" (Jensen-Shannon distance), "ks" (Kolmogorov-Smirnov), "wasserstein" (normalized Wasserstein distance) or "adwin". See dde_feature_drift().

threshold

Drift threshold of the test. NULL uses the default of dde_feature_drift().

window_size

Size of the reference and of the analysis windows (\(r = q\)).

monitoring_step

Number of observations between two consecutive tests of the window-based tests.

confirmation_delay

Number of observations between the first drift signal and the decision on which features drift. NULL (the default) uses half a window. See Details.

thresholds

Correlation thresholds \(z\) at which the DDE curve is evaluated.

score_threshold

Score from which an unmonitored feature is predicted to drift.

update_curve

Whether to refine the DDE curve with the drifts detected after the initialization, by averaging it with the curves of the monitored features (Algorithm 1, line 29).

delta

Confidence of ADWIN, used when test = "adwin".

seed

Seed of the random draw of the monitored features.

Value

dfr_dde object

Details

The detector compares, for each feature, a reference window with the following analysis window, both of window_size observations (Algorithm 1). It starts in an initialization phase in which every feature is monitored. The first drift with at least two drifting features fixes the DDE curve, computed with dde_curve() from the Pearson correlations in the reference window. From then on only the monitored features are tested. When some of them drift, every unmonitored feature gets a drift score with dde_score(), the mean of the DDE curve over its correlations with the drifting monitored features (Eq. 25).

A drift is reported when at least one monitored feature drifts. The features do not cross their thresholds at the same observation, so the first signal opens a confirmation period of confirmation_delay observations, after which the windows are tested again: the drifting features are those of this confirmation test (with ADWIN, every feature signalled during the period), and no drift is reported if none remains. The correlations are measured in the reference window of the first signal. After a drift the analysis window becomes the new reference window.

The fitted object exposes:

  • curve: the current DDE curve (see dde_curve());

  • feature_drift: per feature, the last decision for the monitored features (0 or 1) and the predicted score for the others;

  • predicted_drift: per feature, whether it is detected or predicted to drift in the last drift;

  • detections: one entry per reported drift, with the observation, the drifting monitored features and the predicted scores.

The paper's code (https://github.com/marcellnemeth/DominoDriftEffect) is not public, so the implementation follows the paper. The window tests use the definitions and default thresholds of the Evidently library.

References

Szucs, G. and Nemeth, M. (2025). Domino drift effect approach for probability estimation of feature drift in high-dimensional data. Knowledge and Information Systems, 67, 4597-4621. doi:10.1007/s10115-025-02362-0

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)

# Six features in two correlated groups; the first group drifts.
set.seed(1)
n <- 600
make <- function(n, shift) {
  a <- stats::rnorm(n, shift)
  b <- stats::rnorm(n)
  data.frame(a1 = a + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), a2 = a + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.3),
             a3 = a + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), b1 = b + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.3),
             b2 = b + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.3), b3 = b + stats::rnorm(n, sd = 0.3))
}
stream <- rbind(make(n, 0), make(n, 3), make(n, 3), make(n, 6))

model <- dfr_dde(monitored = c("a1", "b1"), test = "ks", threshold = 1e-3,
                 window_size = 300, monitoring_step = 50)
model <- fit(model, stream)
model$curve
#>    threshold pairs drifting_pairs probability lift
#> 1        0.0    15              3         0.4  1.0
#> 2        0.1     6              3         1.0  2.5
#> 3        0.2     6              3         1.0  2.5
#> 4        0.3     6              3         1.0  2.5
#> 5        0.4     6              3         1.0  2.5
#> 6        0.5     6              3         1.0  2.5
#> 7        0.6     6              3         1.0  2.5
#> 8        0.7     6              3         1.0  2.5
#> 9        0.8     6              3         1.0  2.5
#> 10       0.9     6              3         1.0  2.5
model$feature_drift
#>  a1  a2  a3  b1  b2  b3 
#> 1.0 1.0 1.0 0.0 0.4 0.4
